learn: Every upload passes the AP POLE check in this run: the save keeps the end state valid, EXPORT_PRE handles Max down, and ROW_ORDER (down before up) handles the moves inside a file.

Two steps show why the order matters: 05-Nov (KOREA before JAPAN would give 36 > 30) and 27-Nov (TAIWAN before THAILAND would give 28 > 20, because AP POLE still counts the 202611 THAILAND for 202612).
OPERATION_TYPE is set at the save and compared with the last value AP POLE has: the same period, else the previous period (27-Nov and 27-Dec).
A value set back to the sent value sends nothing (03-Dec 09:30); a change of order type is DELETE + ADD in AP POLE and nothing in GTOPAS (03-Dec 10:00).

Every part in a run has one header row in the Kanban staging: 1 to 4 when the Kanban changed, 5 (ACTION KEEP) when only the destinations changed (05-Nov, 10-Nov 09:30, 03-Dec). A header 5 is replaced when the Kanban changes later (10-Nov 10:00) and is never in the KANBAN file.
GTOPAS gets a row only when a destination appears or disappears for the part, whatever the order type; new-period rows that GTOPAS already has write nothing.
An Inactive part keeps its Kanban row in AP POLE; its destinations get DELETE (0) once, in the first period it is Inactive.
